guide.summary: West Lake sights, Lingyin Temple, the tea and Liangzhu museums and the zoo, with breakfast spots, dinners, cafés and cocktail bars checked against their operators' own websites.
guide.tip: The China National Tea Museum's Shuangfeng site closes on Tuesdays except public holidays, so plan your tea day for another day of the week.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The China National Tea Museum's Shuangfeng site at 88 Longjing Road lists a Tuesday closure, except on public holidays. None of the other places checked here published a weekly closing day.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.value: Book Song and Liangzhu groups ahead
toolkit.copy: Song takes reservations on +86 (571) 8681 8888 or by email. From 12 November 2026, group visits to the Liangzhu Museum must be booked through the “良渚古城” WeChat account or mini program.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Yuan, Steam House and the café at Amanfayun are open to non-residents, subject to availability. The Tea Museum's free tea courses are booked by phone on 0571-87964232 on weekdays.

toolkit.label: Weather rules
toolkit.copy: Lingyin Temple and six other West Lake temples closed temporarily for typhoons in July and August 2026 and reopened by notice. Check the temple's announcements page before you go in stormy weather.

guide.dek: Pair West Lake with Lingyin Temple on one day, keep any day but Tuesday for the tea museum, and book the Michelin-starred dinners ahead.
intro: West Lake is the anchor of this guide. The West Lake Scenic Area Administrative Committee describes a protected area of about 60 square kilometres, and its own pages place Broken Bridge at the eastern end of Bai Causeway and Huagang Guanyu in the lake's southwest corner, east of Su Causeway. You can link the two along the shore and then head west to Lingyin Temple at 1 Fayun Lane, off Lingyin Road. The temple's announcements show it closed temporarily for typhoons in July and August 2026, so check them in stormy weather.

For tea, the China National Tea Museum's Shuangfeng site is at 88 Longjing Road, and its November 2026 notice lists a Tuesday closure, except on public holidays. The museum's Tea Learning Center runs two free public tea courses each week, booked by phone on weekdays from 9:00 to 11:30 and from 14:00 to 17:00. Further out, the Liangzhu Museum is at 1 Meilizhou Road in Yuhang District. From 12 November 2026, groups must book through the “良渚古城” WeChat account or mini program before visiting.

Two Four Seasons hotels anchor the dinners. Jin Sha, at the West Lake hotel on 5 Lingyin Road, kept its one Michelin star in the 2026 guide and builds its Jiangsu-Zhejiang menu around the seasons. The same hotel runs West Lake Bistro for Italian food and a Lobby Lounge with afternoon tea and signature cocktails. Song, on the eighth floor of Four Seasons Hotel Hangzhou at Hangzhou Centre, also holds one star for Ningbo-rooted Zhejiang cooking, and its Autumn Sea Feast menu runs until 14 December 2026. You can reserve on +86 (571) 8681 8888.

For a slower day, Amanfayun sits at 22 Fayun Lane, the same lane as Lingyin Temple, and its venues are open to non-residents subject to availability. Yuan serves from breakfast through to evening drinks, Steam House offers dumplings and village-style steamed dishes at lunch and dinner, and the café sells freshly baked bread, cakes and coffee from morning until dusk. With children, Hangzhou Zoo at 40 Hupao Road opens from 7:00 to 17:00 between October and March, and its ticket window closes at 16:30.
summaryCards: Start at Broken Bridge on Bai Causeway, follow the shore to Huagang Guanyu, and finish at Lingyin Temple on Fayun Lane.
Have breakfast at Yuan or the café at Amanfayun, then visit the China National Tea Museum on any day except Tuesday.
Reserve Jin Sha or Song ahead, and book Liangzhu Museum group visits through the “良渚古城” WeChat account.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Only 17 places could be confirmed, below the 25–35 target: most Hangzhou restaurants, cafés and bakeries publish only through apps or WeChat, and many official sites failed automated reading (403 or 418 responses at several hotel groups and % Arabica, expired or invalid certificates at the Zhejiang Provincial Museum, Hangzhou Grand Theatre, Songcheng, Zhiweiguan and Fuchun Resort, refused connections at Lou Wai Lou, Waipojia, the West Lake State Guest House and Xiling Seal Art Society, and unreadable or garbled pages at the Zhejiang Art Museum, China Academy of Art Museum, Zhejiang Museum of Natural History and Xixi Wetland). The China National Silk Museum was readable but published no street address. Four Seasons venues were checked on the operator's press site because its main site returned 403. Weekly hours were not published for Lingyin Temple, the Tea Museum, Liangzhu Museum or any restaurant; Amanfayun's dining page gives service periods only and no dated 2026 item; the Rooftop Stars Bar hours come from an undated press story and the hotel's fact sheet calls the rooftop bar Stellaris. West Lake's location is given through the committee's address and descriptions rather than a single street address.
